rows.readsAs: a woolly lamb or young sheep with a long snout
rows.defect: Body is a cream fleece-textured barrel on cloven hoof-tipped legs with a thin curled tail and a single low rounded flap ear — none of the aardvark cues survive: no tall rabbit ears, no arched back, no thick tapering kangaroo tail; only the tubular snout is right, and it sits on livestock anatomy.
rows.fix: Swap the fleece body texture for sparse bristly grey-pink hide, straighten the back into a high arch peaking over the hips, replace the curled tail with a thick cone tapering from a wide base, and raise the ears into two tall upright leaf shapes above the skull line.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld; ear description corrected. At 4x the head carries a large flat saucer/disc ear drawn face-on (pale ring around a dark-brown oval, sitting directly over the eye) plus two small triangular points tucked behind it — not one low flap, and nothing resembling tall upright rabbit ears. Topline is dead level from shoulder to rump: no arch, rump is not the high point. Tail is a thin cat-like S-curve held up and clear of the body, not a thick-based tapering kangaroo tail. All four feet terminate in dark two-toed CLOVEN HOOVES with a white nail highlight (visible at 4x on both near legs) where an aardvark needs spade-like digging claws. Body is a cream barrel covered in dense fine-hair fleece strokes; aardvark hide is sparse-haired pinkish grey. Only the long tapering tubular snout with its terminal nostril dot is correct, and it is grafted onto lamb anatomy — a stranger names this a sheep.

rows.readsAs: a speckled green egg or river pebble floating above a shadow
rows.defect: The shell is a fat 3D ovoid rather than a flat ear-shaped plate, and the two other mustReads are entirely absent — no muscular foot underneath and no frilly tentacle fringe at the rim, so the only mollusc cue is the row of pores.
rows.fix: Flatten the shell to a low domed oval seen at a shallow three-quarter angle, seat it on a broad cream muscular foot that bulges out past the shell edge and touches the ground, and ring the exposed mantle margin with short dark tentacle filaments.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld; pore placement is worse than claimed. The shell is a fat domed 3D egg (~1.35:1, not the reference's 2:1 flat plate) with a specular gloss arc running down the upper-right rim, so the surface reads as eggshell rather than nacre. The five dark pores are not along the shell margin at all — they sit in a straight line across the MIDDLE of the face, shrinking left-to-right, which reads as painted dots on an Easter egg rather than the respiratory row that must hug the left edge. The lower rim is a smooth unbroken arc: no muscular foot mass protruding beneath, no mantle skirt, no tentacle fringe at any point on the perimeter, and no aperture or whorl apex. Zero mollusc cues survive.

rows.readsAs: an elephant
rows.defect: The ear is a hard-edged ribbed plate with a dark outline laid flat across the shoulder — it reads as a pasted disc sitting on top of the body rather than a flap growing out of the skull, and its rim seam cuts across the neck.
rows.fix: Attach the ear along a soft blended margin at the skull, taper its lower edge to a thinner ragged lobe, drop the black keyline in favour of a value shift, and let the shoulder texture pass under the ear's leading edge.

rows.readsAs: a lean blotched dog in camouflage markings
rows.defect: The ear reads as one large dark brown curl wrapping over the crown like a horn or hood instead of two tall rounded bat-like ears standing clear of the head.
rows.fix: Split the mass into a single upright ear silhouette with a visible outer rim and darker inner cup, set it forward on the crown so sky shows on both sides of it, and shorten the muzzle slightly so the ear reads oversized against the head.

rows.readsAs: a blue spiny lizard
rows.defect: The tail is a short thick paddle far shorter than the trunk instead of roughly body-length, and the head is an unblended ellipse overlapping the shoulders with a visible seam rather than a blunt triangular skull.
rows.fix: Extend the tail to at least the trunk's length and taper it to a fine tip, and rebuild the head as a wedge that is widest at the jaw hinge and narrows to the snout, merging its rear edge into the neck instead of stacking it on the body.

rows.readsAs: a guinea pig or a hamster
rows.defect: The animal has no legs at all — the body is a smooth rounded blob resting on the ground with a single small dark stub at the rear, so the slender long-legged frame that defines an agouti is entirely missing and the silhouette collapses to a cavy.
rows.fix: Lift the body clear of the ground on four thin upright legs with small dark hoof-like claw tips, and re-shape the back so it climbs continuously from the shoulders to a high rounded rump above the hind limbs.
rows.verifyWhy: Claimed cause REFUTED, verdict stands. There are two legs, not zero: at 7x a bent crouching hind leg with a long flat plantigrade foot sits at lower-left and a short front peg-leg with a rounded foot at lower-right — both painted near-black brown, which is why they vanish against the orange body at 1x. The real identity defect is their form: crouch-folded stubs roughly 15% of body height with the belly nearly resting on the ground, in place of the agouti's long slim upright legs on hoof-like claws (that mustRead is genuinely absent). Compounding it, the two ears are upright pointed triangles (agouti ears are small and rounded), the body is a near-perfect ball whose highest point is mid-back rather than the rump, and a large white incisor pair juts at the mouth — the whole silhouette reads as a crouching rabbit.

rows.readsAs: a plump seagull with its wings spread
rows.defect: The bill is a small light yellow wedge with no bulk, no strong terminal hook and no tube nostrils, so the heaviest identity cue for an albatross is missing and the bird defaults to a generic gull.
rows.fix: Enlarge the bill to roughly head-depth, add a distinct downcurved hooked nail at the tip, and paint the paired tubular nostril ridges as darker horn plates along the sides of the upper mandible.

rows.readsAs: an alligator or crocodile
rows.defect: The tail is a short blunt triangle much shorter than the trunk instead of longer than the body, and the dorsal scute field reads as a flat corrugated rectangle pasted on the back whose upper edge juts past the body contour as a straight shelf.
rows.fix: Lengthen the tail to exceed the trunk and taper it with a laterally compressed profile, and convert the scute panel into rows of individually domed keeled bumps that follow the curve of the spine and die out at the shoulders.

rows.readsAs: a long-tailed brown lizard or skink
rows.defect: The armoured squared scale rows and the lateral skin fold along the flank are absent — the trunk is a smooth spotted oval — and the head is a separate ellipse laid over the shoulders with a visible seam.
rows.fix: Band the trunk with regular rectangular scale rows and cut a darker granular fold line running the full length of the flank between fore and hind limbs, then blend the head's rear margin into the neck and elongate the trunk so it reads as a tube rather than an egg.

rows.readsAs: an alpaca or llama
rows.defect: The fleece reads as a ragged fringe of loose strands hanging off the edges of an otherwise smooth white barrel, with a visible boundary where the shaggy patch stops, rather than dense wool covering the whole body; the ears are small rounded nubs instead of short straight spear shapes.
rows.fix: Carry the crimped wool texture across the whole torso and up the neck so there is no clean patch edge, and rebuild the ears as two narrow straight-sided points angled slightly outward above a distinct topknot fringe.

rows.readsAs: a black spotted salamander
rows.defect: The legs are featureless black stubs with no toes or elbow, and a flat grey slab runs along the back like a pasted rectangle rather than a spine highlight; the yellow spotting also reads as a fire salamander instead of the uniform jet-black the row calls for.
rows.fix: Give each of the four limbs a visible upper/lower segment and 4-5 splayed toes on the ground plane, replace the grey back slab with a soft glossy specular ridge that follows the body curve, and drop the ochre blotches to a sparse few (or remove them) so the skin reads uniformly wet-black.

rows.readsAs: a small pale shrimp
rows.defect: The body is a smooth featureless blob with no segment ridges, and the underside carries only four identical thin bristles instead of the many differently-shaped legs (gnathopods, pereopods) the row requires.
rows.fix: Overlay 7-8 overlapping tergite arcs down the curved back to segment the pereon, and rebuild the underside as a graded series: two stout clawed gnathopods under the head, then thinner walking legs shortening toward the tail.

rows.readsAs: a thick coiled green snake
rows.defect: The dorsal pattern is inverted - the blotches are lighter than the skin and blur out as pale fog spots, so the dark oval saddles that identify an anaconda are absent.
rows.fix: Repaint the markings as hard-edged dark olive-black ovals with paler halos, alternating along the spine and offset onto the flanks, so they read as blotches on olive-green rather than pale highlights.

rows.readsAs: a small silvery needle-snouted fish
rows.defect: The huge underslung gape is missing - the head ends in a solid spike with only a hairline crease, so the mouth never reaches past the eye, and the flank is a uniform mesh-textured white with no distinct bright lateral stripe.
rows.fix: Cut a dark open jawline from the snout tip back to behind the eye with the lower jaw hinged under it, and lay a narrow high-value silver band along the midline against a slightly darker blue-grey dorsum so the stripe separates.

rows.readsAs: a yellow-striped marine angelfish
rows.defect: The face has no mouth at all - just an eye on a blank snout - and no gill-cover spine, and the trailing filaments read as one loose hair arcing past the fish rather than extensions of the dorsal and anal fin tips.
rows.fix: Add a small pursed terminal mouth at the front of the disc plus a short backward spine at the gill-cover corner, and root the filaments in the rear tips of the dorsal and anal fins so they trail from the fin membrane instead of floating past the body.

rows.readsAs: a fanged deep-sea fish beside a floating light
rows.defect: The illicium is invisible - the stalk is a near-black hairline that stops well short of the glow, so the lure reads as a detached orb hovering in the water rather than arching over the mouth from the fish's brow.
rows.fix: Draw the stalk as a visible pale-lit curve rising from the snout and arching forward until it physically meets the bulb, and open the jaw into an upturned crescent so the needle fangs sit inside a real gape instead of hanging off the silhouette edge.

rows.readsAs: a green lizard with a red throat fan
rows.defect: The tail is barely as long as the head and body instead of clearly longer, and the limbs are short dark stubs with no feet - no long slender toes or adhesive pads anywhere.
rows.fix: Roughly double the tail length to a fine whip tapering past the frame's midline, and rebuild each limb with a visible elbow/knee and five long splayed toes ending in widened pads; narrow the skull into a pointed wedge snout.

rows.readsAs: a brown ant
rows.defect: The hind pair of legs sprouts from the gaster instead of the thorax, and only five legs are drawn, so the six-legs-from-the-middle-segment read fails.
rows.fix: Re-anchor all three leg pairs to the underside of the thorax as coxa points spaced along its length, and draw the full six with paired left/right offsets so the abdomen carries no limbs.

rows.readsAs: a tan antelope or gazelle
rows.defect: No tail is drawn on the rump at all, and the horns are smooth tapered cones with no annulation rings, so two named traits are missing.
rows.fix: Add a short dark-tipped flicking tail at the rump and cut 12-15 raised transverse rings up the lower two-thirds of each horn; lighten the underbelly and inner legs to cream so the white belly separates from the tan flank.

rows.readsAs: a small green ant
rows.defect: It is built on the same head-thorax-gaster armature as the Ant render in this batch, only recoloured green - no soft pear-shaped bulb, no cornicle tubes on the rear, and no needle beak or stem, so all three mustReads are absent and it misreads as an ant.
rows.fix: Replace the segmented ant body with one soft teardrop abdomen swelling to its widest point at the rear, add a pair of short dark tube cornicles projecting up from the back of that abdomen with a small cauda between them, shorten the antennae, and plant a fine needle rostrum from the head into a green stem the aphid straddles.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld, and the claimed cause checks out under magnification. The body is three hard-edged spheres pinched at two waists — round head, egg thorax, and a rear ovoid ruled with vertical banding (a wasp/ant gaster texture) — not one soft pear bulb. Nothing projects from the abdomen rear except a single knee-bent hind leg (the '7' shape past the right edge of the gaster); there is no cornicle pair, and worse, two of the six legs are rooted in the abdomen instead of the thorax, so the one place a cornicle belongs is already occupied by a misplaced leg. The head carries a large glossy cartoon eye and two long kinked antennae with only a tiny nub at the front of the muzzle — no downward-angled rostrum — and the frame is empty background, so there is no stem to be pierced. Overlaid on Ant.png the silhouette, leg splay, antenna sweep and shadow ellipse match; only the hue (green vs brown) and a slightly larger thorax differ. A stranger names this a green ant.

rows.readsAs: a large green scaly river fish
rows.defect: the dorsal and anal fins are drawn UNDER the body as low-contrast dark ghosts at mid-body, so instead of framing the tail far back they read as shadows bleeding out above and below the silhouette; no red-edged rear scales and no mouth line at all on the snout
rows.fix: move the dorsal and anal fin masses back to the last quarter of the body so they bracket the caudal paddle, draw them at full body opacity in front of the silhouette, tint the rear third of the scale field with red scale edges, and add a short upward-angled mouth line at the snout tip

rows.readsAs: a golden bream or sunfish
rows.defect: the body is a deep near-circular disc with a curved back and no black wedge bars anywhere, and the dorsal is a sawtooth crown floating on the mid-back with its base tucked behind the body outline; none of the archerfish signature survives
rows.fix: flatten the topline to a straight sloping ramp running down to an upturned mouth, drop aspect to ~2.5, paint 4-5 bold black downward wedge bars on a silver flank, and move the dorsal back near the tail with its base merged into the dorsal contour
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld, but one stated cause is wrong. Measured silhouette is 193x139 px = aspect 1.39 against a required 2.5: a symmetric almond/discus pointed at BOTH ends with an evenly convex back, so the flat straight sloping topline to an upturned mouth never happens (the mouth is only a 1px dark scratch rising toward the snout tip). The flank is uniform olive-khaki - twelve samples along the midline all fall between lum 125 and 197 with no tonal break - so the bold black wedge bars are wholly absent and the 'silver' body is olive. The dorsal is a flat dull-olive (81,80,57) comb of five isolated sharp triangles with no webbing between spines, spanning x=185-283, i.e. the middle ~60% of the back, where the mustRead wants it set far back near the tail. REFUTED sub-claim: the comb is not floating - vertical scans show its base sits flush on the topline at every x (crown colour ends exactly where body pixels begin at x=205, 255 and 283), it is simply drawn behind the body. Fix the comb's shape and its forward placement, not a gap. Currently reads as a discus/sunfish.

rows.readsAs: a slim pale cod-like fish
rows.defect: no chin barbel is visible at all, and the dorsal fins are faint grey humps drawn behind the body rather than distinct fins on the back
rows.fix: add a single short barbel hanging from the lower jaw and redraw the dorsals as opaque separate fins sitting on top of the dorsal line; deepen the tail fork slightly

rows.readsAs: a white dog or small white wolf
rows.defect: the muzzle is long, thin and greyhound-pointed and the single ear is a flat dark triangle that reads as a hole punched in the skull, the opposite of the short blunt muzzle and rounded ears the row calls for; the brush tail is a grey striped plume overlapping the flank rather than joining the rump
rows.fix: shorten the muzzle by about a third and round the tip, replace the dark triangle with two short white rounded ears with pale inner shading, and re-anchor the tail at the rump with its base blended into the hip fur

rows.readsAs: a white pet rabbit
rows.defect: ear tips are pink/grey with no black, and the ears are the tall narrow rabbit shape rather than the short hare ear; the hind foot is a small grey stub with no visible oversize
rows.fix: shorten and thicken the ears and cap the top third of each in solid black, and enlarge the hind foot into a long broad pad planted under the haunch

rows.readsAs: an armadillo or banded anteater
rows.defect: the banding runs as evenly spaced stripes across the entire back with no distinct solid shoulder and hip shields, and the body is long and flat like a dachshund rather than domed, so the armour reads as painted fur stripes
rows.fix: give the shell a domed profile, replace the front and rear thirds of the stripe field with two solid unbanded scute shields, and confine the hinged bands to the middle of the back; add ridged scute rings to the tail

rows.readsAs: a featureless cigar or pill shape with an eye
rows.defect: the body is a straight-sided torpedo ringed by a closed grey halo outline instead of ribbon fins, the mouth is a straight downward-slanted slit with no upturn, there are no barbels, and the tail is a vestigial wisp so the body effectively ends in nothing
rows.fix: taper the body and give it a real forked/paddle tail, break the grey halo into distinct long ribbon dorsal and anal fins running from mid-body to the tail, cut the mouth as a steeply upturned drawbridge slot, and add two barbels projecting forward from the chin
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld, but two stated causes are wrong. REFUTED: the mouth slit does NOT slant downward - it runs from about (297,203) up to (335,192), a slight UPWARD slant; the real defect is that it is a 1px hairline drawn on a blunt vertical-cut snout wall, so the steeply upturned drawbridge gape is absent as a shape, not as a direction. REFUTED: the grey is not a closed halo - there are genuinely separate dorsal and anal ribbons (flat slate 76,81,81 bands about 7px deep, y=171-177 above and y=210-216 below at x=250) running the body length; they fail because they are the same flat grey as the cast shadow, of constant thickness, with no rays and no taper, so at size they read as a rim outline rather than fins. UPHELD: no barbels anywhere on the chin, and the body is a plank - the silhouette top holds y=171 dead flat from x=200 to x=300 - ending in a guillotine-flat rounded-rectangle wall whose caudal fin is a ~10px dark olive thorn plus near-invisible hairline rays. Two of three mustReads absent; reads as a bar of soap with an eye.

rows.readsAs: an elephant
rows.defect: the ear is an oversized dark ribbed oval pasted between head and shoulder with a hard rim, reading African-sized and detached rather than the small triangular Asian ear
rows.fix: shrink the ear to roughly half its size, reshape it to a rounded triangle that hugs the cheek, soften its rim and blend its base into the head so it stops reading as a separate disc; add the twin forehead domes with a dip between

rows.readsAs: a small penguin or razorbill
rows.defect: the white front is a flat hard-edged decal ellipse sitting on the black body with no feather blending, and the wing is indistinguishable from the dark tail wedge jutting out behind
rows.fix: feather the edge of the white breast into the black flanks and give the wing its own stubby outlined shape held against the side, distinct from the tail; darken the bill toward razorbill grey-black

rows.readsAs: a white shorebird chick with a dagger bill, like a small tern
rows.defect: the bill is a straight thick-based yellow dagger angled DOWNWARD instead of a thin needle sweeping strongly up, and the plumage is entirely white-grey with no black pied markings, so both identity traits are gone; the flank is a set of concentric grey rings that read as a target swirl
rows.fix: replace the bill with a very thin needle that sweeps sharply upward and darken it to black, add the black crown/nape and black wing panels of the pied pattern, redraw the wing as one clean folded shape instead of concentric rings, and recolour the legs blue-grey
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld, but the bill direction is misreported. REFUTED: the bill is not angled downward - its centreline holds y=136.5-137 across its whole run from tip (x=79) to base (x=146), i.e. dead level with zero curvature. The actual defect is that it is a short, thick, straight golden-yellow (224,177,60) triangular wedge 12px deep at the base with no upward recurve at all, and the wrong colour - an avocet's is black and needle-thin. UPHELD: no black anywhere on the bird except the 3px eye; the darkest plumage pixel sampled is 91,92,93 mid-grey on the wing, so the black cap, nape and wing panels of the pied pattern are entirely missing. The legs are ochre-yellow (201,162,79) where the mustRead calls for long blue-grey. UPHELD: the flank is a mid-grey annulus enclosing a white oval, reading as a target ring / spiral rather than a folded wing. Bbox 288x211 = aspect 1.36 vs 1.8, so it is also too squat. Reads as a generic white gull or tern chick.

rows.readsAs: a pink axolotl / larval salamander
rows.defect: the tail fin is a dull grey-mauve ellipse pasted behind the pink tail with a hard seam — it reads as a detached shadow blob, and no fin crest continues along the back
rows.fix: replace the grey ellipse with a translucent pink-tinted fin membrane that fairs continuously out of the tail and runs forward as a low crest along the spine, sharing the body's palette

rows.readsAs: a small dark monkey in shadow
rows.defect: all three signature traits are absent — the huge naked bat ears are only a faint white outline hugging the skull, there is no elongated wire middle finger, and the tail is a thin smooth curl far smaller than the body
rows.fix: add oversized bare rounded ears standing clear of the head silhouette, splay one forehand with a visibly skeletal extra-long middle digit, and thicken the tail into a plumed mass wider than the torso; lift the fur value so the silhouette separates from the background
rows.verifyWhy: Claimed ear-cause is wrong: the white arc over the crown is not an ear attempt at all, it is a rim-light stroke that traces the ENTIRE silhouette (crown, both torso flanks, under the belly). The real ears are two tiny eye-sized round brown nubs half-buried in the head fluff (one at ~x255,y158) - present but rendered as small round macaque ears instead of enormous naked bat petals. Middle finger: no hand exists anywhere - both forelimbs are plain dark tapered cylinders ending in blunt rounded tips with zero digits. Tail: a smooth matte-brown tube the same width as an arm with a blunt rounded tip and no shag, and its root fuses into the left arm mass so it reads as sprouting from the armpit rather than the rump; its mass is roughly a quarter of the torso, not larger. Net read: a dark baby macaque with big white-ringed eyes and a pink muzzle.

rows.readsAs: a generic tan macaque or capuchin
rows.defect: the face is a flat forward-facing disc with no muzzle at all — the long dog-like snout that defines a baboon is entirely missing, and the tail is a smooth even arc with no basal kink
rows.fix: project a long downward-sloping dog muzzle from the face with the eyes set close together high on it, kink the tail sharply upward for the first third then drop it straight, and add a shaggy shoulder cape
rows.verifyWhy: Muzzle claim confirmed at zoom: the head is a flat frontal tan circle with zero snout projection - a two-dot nose and a curved smiling mouth line painted flat on the disc, round ears stuck on both sides, and the eyes are WIDE-set (the reference calls for close-set), giving a cartoon-monkey / human-baby face. Tail claim confirmed and extended: it is a uniform-width blunt-tipped C-arc with no basal kink, and its root never meets a rump - it merges into the left arm at the shoulder, so the tail appears to grow out of the armpit. Third mustRead also absent: no shoulder cape, the torso is a smooth pale gourd with soft blotches. Reads as a plush toy macaque.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy camel
rows.defect: the two humps barely separate — the shaggy straw texture is a single pasted patch with a visible hard edge on the flank that merges both humps into one lumpy mass
rows.fix: deepen the saddle between the humps so two distinct crowns break the topline, and feather the shaggy texture patch into the body edge instead of ending it on a straight seam

rows.readsAs: a thylacine or striped ferret
rows.defect: heavy dark vertical bars band the whole flank and back, which overrides the badger read entirely; the face carries no continuous white stripe running back over the crown and the feet are pale stubs with no digging claws
rows.fix: drop the vertical barring for a grizzled grey coat, paint one bold white stripe from the nose over the crown down the neck with black cheek bands either side, and give the forefeet long straight pale claws
rows.verifyWhy: Stripe claim confirmed: ~20 heavy dark vertical bars run shoulder-to-rump over the whole flank plus one horizontal mid-flank line, and the bars continue across the muzzle - a thylacine/tiger coat, and the head is white with dark bars crossing it, the exact inverse of a badger mask (no longitudinal white crown stripe). But the claim misses the dominant defect: a large background-navy circular HOLE is punched clean through the skull just behind and above the eye (~x300,y155), reading as a missing chunk of head rather than an eye patch or ear. Feet are worse than 'pale stubs' - each leg terminates as an OPEN CYLINDER with a visible grey elliptical end-cap like cut pipe, no foot, toe or claw geometry at all. Legs are also long and spindly with a wide gap under the belly, so the silhouette is a long-legged striped dog, not a low-slung badger.

rows.readsAs: a banana slug (or, at a glance, a banana)
rows.defect: the head end is a small jagged spike cluster rather than two clean pairs of tentacles with eye knobs on the upper tips, and the body is a featureless flat lens with no mantle saddle or pneumostome
rows.fix: draw four distinct smooth stalks — long upper pair with dark eye beads, short lower feelers — and add an oval mantle saddle behind the head with a small dark breathing hole on its right side

rows.readsAs: a brown wild ox / banteng
rows.defect: the white rump patch is missing — the hindquarters are the same brown as the body — and there is no white band above the muzzle
rows.fix: add a clean white patch across the rump and under the tail base, and a pale band over the top of the muzzle; keep the existing white leg socks as the anchor for the pattern

rows.readsAs: a barnacle cone (reads slightly like a small lampshade)
rows.defect: no feathery cirri sweep out of the summit opening — the aperture is just a small dark slot, so the shape reads as inert shell rather than a living animal
rows.fix: paint a curled fan of fine feathery cirri arcing out of the trapdoor slot, and taper the plate seams so they converge unevenly at the summit instead of running as straight ruled lines

rows.readsAs: a barracuda / pike-like predatory fish
rows.defect: the teeth read as a pasted sawtooth comb hanging below a flat jaw line rather than daggers set in an underslung lower jaw, and the two dorsal fins are soft grey smudges with no fin edge
rows.fix: open the jaw slightly with the lower jaw projecting past the upper, set fewer, longer, irregular fangs interlocking along both jaws, and redraw both dorsals as crisp-edged triangular fins in the body's silver

rows.readsAs: a deep-sea fish with a clear bubble helmet — a barreleye
rows.defect: the tubular eyes are a single flat green rectangle inside the dome, and the two dark scent pits sit on that block instead of on the front of the snout, so the anatomy reads as one pasted box
rows.fix: split the green mass into two upward-pointing cylindrical barrels with lens caps on top, and move the two dark nostril pits forward onto the snout below the dome where they read as false eyes

rows.readsAs: a scaled bony fish with a flat grey satellite dish pasted over its face
rows.defect: the gaping mouth is drawn as a hard-outlined closed ellipse plastered across the entire head, with the eye floating inside the ring and no snout, jaw depth or shark body behind it (forked scaly-fish tail, fins reduced to dark blobs hidden behind the flank)
rows.fix: replace the face-plate disc with an open jaw built from the silhouette: carry the pointed conical snout forward past the mouth, hinge the lower jaw down so the mouth cavity is a dark interior between upper and lower rims, move the eye out onto the head above and behind the gape, and re-cut the body as a shark (smooth skin, heterocercal tail, drooping dorsal raised clear of the topline)
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld, but the claim is partly wrong about the body and fins. The real defect is the head: the body's forward silhouette simply ends and a face-on ellipse (~90x125px, ~28% of body length) with a hard bright-white 2px stroke is pasted over the terminus, filled with horizontal pale bands and a pale triangular wedge. There is no snout forward of the mouth, no lower jaw, no head taper — the mouth ring IS the head. The eye (white ring, dark pupil) sits INSIDE that aperture in its upper-left quadrant, painted on the mouth's interior fill instead of on head skin behind the mouth corner, and the ellipse is drawn in face-on projection while the body is strict side profile, so the two halves of the animal are in different views. CORRECTIONS to the claim: the shark body IS present behind the mouth and the long gill slits read correctly (4-5 dark curved strokes wrapping the flank), and the fins are NOT dark blobs hidden behind the flank — the dorsal is a plainly visible mid-gray rounded loaf-shaped mound sitting above the topline with no apex and no trailing edge, mirrored by an identical rounded blob under the belly, so it reads as a shadow lump rather than the large drooping dorsal. Still true and still wrong: the caudal is a symmetric tuna-style deep V with straight lobes (not a shark's lunate/heterocercal tail) and thin stray ray-lines bleed out past the fin edge into open water, and the flank is covered in a regular diamond scale field — bony-fish scales on a shark.

rows.readsAs: a green bass or perch
rows.defect: the spiny front dorsal is a row of separate zigzag triangles hovering above the back with a visible gap, so it reads pasted on and never joins the soft rear dorsal
rows.fix: seat the spine row into the topline and connect the spines with a membrane that runs continuously back into the soft dorsal; also deepen the jaw line into the large hinged bucket mouth the row calls for

rows.readsAs: male lion in side profile
a sea urchin or spiky red-and-white grub

rows.readsAs: a spotted lizard or salamander

rows.readsAs: a neat symmetrical rosette of pointed green leaves, like a young dracaena or aloe

rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld. rows.readsAs: a fountain of dry straw-coloured reeds or an ornamental grass clump

rows.readsAs: a palm tree — woody forked trunk with feathery pinnate fronds

rows.readsAs: a tuft of golden grass with one small seed head — reads as wheat or an ornamental grass

rows.readsAs: a tall columnar cactus — a saguaro or organ pipe — with a yellow daisy on top

rows.readsAs: a bundle of bare brown twigs topped with white pom-pom flowers — a dried arrangement, not an evergreen

rows.readsAs: a generic vine with round leaves and small pink flecks of blossom

rows.readsAs: a slim herb with paired narrow leaves and a thin lilac flower spike

rows.readsAs: a dense pale grey-green foliage column or bottlebrush of leaves
rows.defect: the flower spike is vestigial - only three tiny purple slivers peek above a tall dense stack of leaves that dominates the whole picture - so the hooded blue-purple flowers, the identity trait, do not read at all, and no hood shape is visible on any flower
rows.fix: cut the leaf stack back to the lower third of the plant and make the upper two thirds a stiff spike of a dozen large deep blue-purple flowers, each drawn with a distinct arched helmet hood overhanging the lower petals; darken and gloss the leaves and cut them into narrow palmate toothed segments
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld, and the leaf trait is wrong too (claim only named the flowers). Fix: raise the flower spike to at least a third of the plant on a visible central rachis, build each flower as a large hood arc capping a paler lower flower, and thin/separate the leaf tiers so cut palmate leaves read individually.

rows.readsAs: a bare brown twig shrub carrying clusters of red berries
rows.defect: the trait is inverted - the main stems are woody brown instead of green jointed rods, and the plant is hung with fleshy red berry clusters plus scattered short green sticks that read as detached floating shards, so the bare green broom with no foliage does not read
rows.fix: recolour every stem yellow-green to olive and make them the only structure - straight upright rods with visibly swollen nodes ringed by a small brown paper collar - delete the loose green shards entirely and replace the red berry clusters with a few tiny buff papery cones sitting at the joints
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld, and the green sticks are worse than 'scattered shards' — at 4x they are uniform-width olive rods with square-cut ends that cross OVER and BEHIND the brown canes at random angles mid-length, several hanging in empty black space touching nothing; they read as spilled straw or pine-needle litter, not stems. The plant body is ~8 smooth tapering chocolate-brown woody canes fanning from a thick brown trunk, with zero joints, zero swollen nodes and zero scale collars anywhere along their length, so the jointed-rod identity is not merely inverted in colour, the node structure was never drawn. At five cane tips sit tight bunches of 6-7 glossy crimson spheres with white specular highlights — ripe fleshy fruit, reading as sumac/elderberry, where the reference wants small dry papery tan cones. Fix: make the canes themselves the green olive rods (the current brown must go), draw a paler swollen band with a small paper collar every ~30px along each rod, delete the loose green sticks entirely, and swap the berry clusters for a few dull tan papery cone scales sitting at the joints.

rows.readsAs: an upright blueberry bush with blue-purple berries
rows.defect: the berries hang in tight clusters of four to six at the shoot tips rather than singly in the leaf axils, and the twigs are brown woody bars instead of the green angled stems named in the row
rows.fix: break the clusters apart so single bloomed berries sit one per leaf axil along the stems, recolour the twigs green with visible angular kinks at each node, and warm a portion of the foliage toward scarlet to carry the autumn note

rows.readsAs: an upright small-leaved bush with red berry clusters
rows.defect: the habit is wrong and the silhouette is a recolour of Mountain Blueberry in this same batch - a tall upright vase of brown stems instead of a low creeping evergreen mat, and the leaves are flat pointed ovals with no rolled edge, notched tip or glossy highlight
rows.fix: redraw as a low spreading mat: short stems arching outward and down from a creeping horizontal runner, wide rather than tall, with small thick glossy leaves showing a notched tip and a dark rolled-under edge, and the scarlet berries nodding in tight clusters at the shoot ends

rows.readsAs: a single fern frond with a tiny white bead spike at the tip
rows.defect: None of the mint signature is drawn: no square branching stem, no flat domed white flower clusters, no silvery bracts — the flowers are a 6-bead vertical string and the leaves sit as regular pinnate lances along one axis, so the whole plant reads as a fern frond rather than a mint.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a branching square-sectioned stem with 2-3 side branches, each tipped by a flat domed corymb of many tiny white purple-speckled florets, and whiten the top pairs of leaves/bracts under each head; keep opposite leaf pairs but shorten and space them so the stem is visible.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld. The plant is a single unbranched vertical stem carrying ten evenly-spaced opposite pairs of plain lance leaves that all tilt upward at the same 40-degree angle — a textbook pinnate frond (ash leaf / fern), not a square branching mint stem with separated leaf tiers. The harvest is a vertical chain of about eight small white beads stacked one above the other on the bare stem tip above the foliage, reading as a bead necklace or a grass spikelet; there is no flat domed corymb, no horizontal spread, no purple speckling, and no silvery bract collar under any head. Leaf colour is uniform mid-green with a pale central midrib streak — the whitish dusting on the upper leaves near the flowers is absent, so the two whitened cues (bracts + upper-leaf bloom) that separate mint from a fern frond both read as zero.

rows.readsAs: a small palm or cycad with one yellow ribbed fruit at the crown
rows.defect: The crown is built from feather-pinnate palm fronds instead of the deeply lobed palmate hands papaya needs, and only one fruit hangs at the crown rather than a cluster hugging the trunk, so it reads generic-palm.

rows.readsAs: a low mound of round cabbage-like leaves with a thin red seed spike
rows.defect: The basal leaves are fused into one solid overlapping dome with no visible stalks, so the red leaf stalks — a named mustRead — are entirely absent, and the seed spike reads as round beads rather than flat papery discs.

rows.readsAs: a leafless wire chevron with five pink daisies stuck on the ends
rows.defect: There is no foliage at all — the plant is bare crossing stems in a rigid geometric V/X lattice, and the flowers are radiating daisy discs instead of dense rounded lipped heads, so nothing about it reads as thyme.
rows.fix: Crowd tiny paired oval grey-green leaves densely along every stem, replace the daisy discs with compact rounded heads of small two-lipped rose-purple florets, and break the straight lattice into softly arching creeping shoots hugging a wider-than-tall mat.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld, with the cause refined: it is not literally bare — there ARE short crossbar segments meant as the paired leaves, but they are drawn as straight olive twigs of the same width and colour as the stems, so at full size zero leaf shape reads and the plant is a rigid symmetric chevron lattice of straight lines rising from one ground point, like a folding trellis or a wire garden frame. The flowers are five identical 12-petal radiating daisies with a dark olive-brown centre disc, evenly spaced along the top of the V — those read as asters/echinacea, not the dense rounded lipped heads of thyme. Nothing gives the creeping woody mat texture; the aspect is wide but the silhouette is geometric, not sprawling.

rows.readsAs: a white feathery bottlebrush or frosted plume

rows.verifyWhy: Upheld. Every leaf lobe on the plant is the same chalk grey-white on its face — the silver felt has been applied to the whole leaf instead of only the underside, so the dark-green upper surface that should dominate a frontal view is nowhere in the picture and the plant reads as frost-killed, dusty, or a dried pampas plume. Geometry compounds it: the leaves are stacked as eight identical radially-symmetric whorls threaded on one vertical axis, each a full starburst of pointed lobes, forming a solid tapering bottlebrush column rather than alternate cut leaves spaced up a stem. rows.readsAs: a fruit tree hung with dark purple berries
rows.defect: The berries render as flat dark rectangular patches with dots pasted onto the canopy rather than elongated knobbly drupes, and the trunk is a bare rectangle with no crooked branches, so the broad spreading crooked crown never reads.

rows.readsAs: a green bottlebrush or foxtail with a speck of yellow at the top

The real defects: no beaked seed pods anywhere on the plant, and the foliage is a dense uniform column of identical small yellow-green spikes packed edge-to-edge around the stem in nine radial whorls, with zero size gradient — no big lyre-shaped lower leaves, no branching stem, no alternate spacing. rows.readsAs: a tropical tree with feathery compound leaves and a few golden fruits
rows.defect: The pinnate sprays radiate stiffly outward like spokes from the canopy blob instead of drooping, the leaflets are straight rather than sickle-curved and toothed, and no white flower sprays appear anywhere.

rows.readsAs: a smooth green corn cob or a stacked column of plain leaves

At 4x the leaves are elongated smooth-edged ovals with a single faint midrib, packed opposite in eight pairs with no gap at all between tiers, so the whole plant fuses into one solid rounded green cylinder — it reads as a corn cob in husk or a pine-cone-shaped succulent. rows.readsAs: a small palm tree on a forked trunk — nearly the same picture as Mountain Papaya in this batch
rows.defect: It is drawn with a thick forked brown trunk, directly contradicting the defining mustRead that there is no visible trunk and the fronds erupt from mud; the fruit head is a small pale knob tucked in the crown instead of a big brown spiky cannonball at ground level.

A thick smooth brown Y-forked trunk occupies the lower two-thirds of the frame, about 190px tall and 40px wide with rounded cap ends, lifting the frond crown well clear of the ground — a direct inversion of the defining mustRead that there is no visible trunk and the fronds erupt from mud. The fronds themselves are acceptable — stiff once-pinnate with regular narrow leaflets fanning from one point — so the fix is the trunk and the fruit, not the foliage.

rows.readsAs: a generic small fruit tree with glowing pale-yellow berries — lemon or apricot, not nutmeg

Crown is one soft hazy green ball, wider than tall, with mid-green elliptic leaves poking out radially — no conical taper and no dark tone (it is the same lit mid-green as every other generic tree). rows.readsAs: a nondescript broadleaf shade tree with brown berries in it

rows.readsAs: wheat or barley — a cereal clump topped by a single tight ear
rows.defect: The seed head is exactly the compact ribbed ear the reference forbids: one narrow vertical spike hugging the culm, with none of the loose open panicle or teardrop spikelets dangling on fine threads that separate oats from wheat.

rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld. The base clump is a decent cream-gold grass fountain, but the harvest is a single narrow vertical ribbed spike about a quarter of the image tall, drawn tight against the top of the culm with a small bristle fan at its tip — the compact ear the reference explicitly forbids. There are no panicle side-branches, no threads, and no dangling teardrop spikelets anywhere; the silhouette is wheat/barley, not oats.

rows.readsAs: a pink-flowered shrub of upright wands — plausibly oleander

rows.readsAs: an olive tree — narrow grey-green leaves with dark round fruits

rows.readsAs: a clump of ornamental grass or an agapanthus — a flowering tuft, no vegetable
rows.defect: There is no bulb at all: the blades rise straight out of flat soil with no swollen papery-skinned bulb and no fringe of wiry roots, and the leaves are flat tapering blades rather than round hollow tubes.

The claim also missed the flower: there IS a harvest element — a flat white disc on a bare stalk above the clump — but it reads as a mushroom cap or an edge-on daisy, not a spherical allium umbel.

rows.readsAs: an orange tree — dense green crown hung with round orange fruit
rows.defect: The mustRead white five-petal blossoms alongside the ripe fruit are entirely absent, and the leaves are plain ovals with no winged stalk or rind pitting on the fruit.

rows.readsAs: a single fern frond or a young seedling stalk — no orchid, no pods

rows.fix: Hang two hand-like clusters of 4-6 long slender green pods from the upper stem joints, thicken the leaves into fleshy waxy oblongs alternating on a leaning vining stem, and add pale aerial roots curling out at each node onto a bark strip.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld. The whole plant is one bare rigid vertical stalk carrying about eleven pairs of small flat lanceolate leaflets angled upward — a fern frond or bracken sprig silhouette. Not one bean-like pod hangs anywhere; the leaves are thin flat blades with no fleshy thickness or waxy sheen; there are no aerial roots and no bark or host to grip; and the stem is dead-straight upright with no vining lean. The render is also very small and dim within the 440px frame, roughly half the height the other flora fill.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond or a single leafy stalk with one white speck on top
rows.defect: It reads as one unbranched ladder of oversized paired leaves — no branching bushy habit, the stem is round and green rather than square and reddish, and the flowering is a single tiny white blob instead of airy flat-topped sprays.
rows.fix: Branch the plant into 3-4 stems from the base, shrink the leaves to small opposite ovals spaced up reddish square stems with visible hairs, and top each stem with a wide flat-topped spray of tiny pink-white florets over dark purple bracts.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld. A single unbranched vertical stem carries about ten pairs of large overlapping lance-shaped leaves stacked as a symmetrical ladder that fills the frame — no side branches, no bushy habit, and the leaves are frond-sized rather than the small opposite ovals of oregano. The stem is a plain round mid-green cylinder with no square edge, no reddish tint, no hairs. The flowering is one small white crescent tuft sitting at the apex only, so there are no airy branched flat-topped sprays and no dark purple bracts. Reads as a fern or a young sapling, not a culinary herb.

rows.readsAs: a pale ornamental grass tuft with a tiny beaded spike — indistinguishable from the Oats render in this same batch
rows.defect: The huge silvery-white feather plume that is the entire identity of pampas is absent, replaced by a short bead-chain spike barely clearing the blades, so the picture collapses to a generic grass clump.
rows.fix: Replace the spike with a large soft feather plume — a fluffy silver-white teardrop of fine radiating filaments — carried on a bare stalk that lifts it a full clump-height above the leaves, and add saw-tooth edges to the arching blades.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld, with the claim's geometry corrected: the plume stalk does clear the blade tips, but what sits on it is a short vertical chain of about a dozen small white beads roughly a tenth of the image tall — a hyacinth-like bead spike, not a huge silky feather. No plume width, no fringe, no silvery sheen, so the defining silhouette is absent. The clump underneath is actually good (dense fountain of long arching saw-edged blades) but is cream-tan rather than blue-grey green, so with the plume gone the picture collapses to a clump of dried straw grass.

rows.readsAs: a small forked palm or cycad with one tiny orange gourd tucked in the crown
rows.defect: none of the three mustReads exist: leaves are soft feathery pinnate fronds rather than long spiral-set sword straps, there is no prop-root cone at all (the trunk just plugs into the ground), and the fruit is a marble-sized orange egg instead of a big knobbly segmented ball — and the render is near-identical to Papaya in this same batch
rows.fix: replace the pinnate fronds with stiff unbranched strap blades whorled in visible 3-rank spiral tiers around the stem tip, add a splayed cone of stilt roots lifting the trunk clear of the soil, and enlarge the fruit to a segmented pineapple-like head hanging below the crown
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld, and the near-identity to Papaya is confirmed: same Y-forked brown trunk, same fan of ~14 feathery pinnate fronds, same fruit blob at the fork crotch — only the leaf hue differs (pale grey-green here vs mid-green on Papaya). Additionally the trunk forks into two limbs at ~55% height, which is wrong for screwpine's own habit and is the root of the shared-geometry problem. Reads as a generic cycad/palm.

rows.readsAs: a young palm with a forked trunk
rows.defect: the trunk forks into two branches (papaya is strictly unbranched and ring-scarred), the crown is feathery pinnate fronds instead of huge deeply lobed palmate blades on long stalks, and there is a single pea-sized fruit at the fork rather than a cluster of melons packed against the trunk under the crown

rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld exactly as claimed. The trunk forks into two limbs at ~55% height (the second limb angles up-right past the crown), directly contradicting the unbranched ring-scarred trunk mustRead; the trunk is also flat mid-brown with no leaf-ring scars. The harvest is one ~35px orange striped ovoid sitting in the crotch of the fork, not a cluster of melons packed against the trunk under the crown. Shares its geometry wholesale with the Pandanus Fruit card in this batch.

rows.readsAs: a dry fountain-shaped clump of grass or young bamboo
rows.defect: the defining firework umbel is absent — every culm ends in a bare arching tip with only a few stray dashes, so nothing at the top reads as a starburst of drooping threads; colour is also dried straw-gold rather than bright green
rows.fix: cap each culm with a dense radiating spray of 40+ fine green threads drooping into a globe, keep the stems bare and straight-vertical, and shift the palette to bright green
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld; refine the cause. Every one of the ~10 arching culms terminates in a bare tapering hook with nothing on it. The silhouette is a symmetric fountain (culms sweeping out and down to left and right, tips below the crown apex) rather than tall vertical stems each capped by a starburst. Colour is dried straw-gold throughout with no bright green anywhere. Reads as a clump of dried pampas or marram grass.

rows.readsAs: a clump of arching green grass
rows.defect: same missing umbel — the stems arch outward and terminate in bare points with no starburst of rays at the top, and the image is the Papyrus render recoloured green rather than a distinct organism

rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld. The silhouette is the Papyrus card's exact geometry — same fountain of ~10 arching culms from a single point base, same arch curvatures, same scatter of short horizontal dashes at the same mid-culm positions — recoloured mid-green; the two cards are distinguishable only by hue. Each culm ends in a bare tapering point, so there is no starburst of thin drooping rays at any tip. Nothing indicates water: the base is a plain ellipse ground shadow, not a waterline. No pale young shoots at the base to carry the 'Shoots' harvest read either.

rows.readsAs: a generic purple-flowered climbing vine

FAIL stands on the appendage geometry instead. (1) The 'cilia' are ~40 perfectly vertical, evenly spaced, equal-length straight hairlines drawn INSIDE the membrane, all parallel to each other rather than normal to the rim, and they stop short of the rim instead of emerging past it — this reads as machine hatching / a barbecue grill, and is the single largest mark area in the picture. Sibling microbe-h1-s10 in this same batch draws its flagella as proper sine curves, so the organic bar is achievable in this family. Fix: give the cilia radial orientation normal to the ellipse rim with length jitter and let them cross the membrane; curve the flagella and start them at the rim rather than ruling one line through the whole body.
